Both images on this manifest were downsized from the Wikimedia Commons originals using macOS sips (no edits to content) so the served file fits a web budget; the raw Wikimedia file is the authoritative source for any reuse.

images.caption: Map of Bangalore, 1854. Surveyed by the Trigonometrical Survey of India, published by Pharaoh and Co., Madras. The full sheet covers both the old walled Pete (centre-left) and the British Civil and Military Station (Cantonment, centre-right), with the connected chain of kere — Dharmambudhi, Sampangi, Halsoor, Sankey, Kempambudhi and dozens of smaller tanks — drawn in their period-correct positions.
images.credit: Surveyed for the Pharaoh atlas; engraved by J. & C. Walker; published Pharaoh and Co. Madras, 1854.
images.processing: Downsized to 2000px wide, JPEG quality 82, via macOS sips. No edits to image content.

images.caption: Ulsoor (Halsoor) Lake, Bangalore, 1834. Steel engraving by William Miller after an original by Humphrey Jervis. Shows the kere full, with the bund visible at right and a temple complex on the shore — the working state of a Bengaluru kere a generation before the Cantonment Water Works (Hesaraghatta dam, 1894) made piped supply the city's primary water source.
images.credit: Engraved by William Miller (1796-1882) after Humphrey Jervis, 1834.
images.processing: Downsized to 1800px wide, JPEG quality 85, via macOS sips. No edits to image content.
